summary: 工作与等待输入颜色相近，错过输入请求
body:
### Problem

The agent status dots on workspaces, tabs and agent rows use four Tailwind colors (`StatusIndicator.tsx`):

| status | color | animation |
|---|---|---|
| working | `amber-500` | static |
| permission (needs input) | `yellow-500` | pulsing |
| failed | `red-500` | pulsing |
| review (done, unread) | `green-500` | static |

`amber-500` and `yellow-500` are close enough that "working" and "needs input" differ mostly by the pulse, which is easy to miss on a 6px dot. Green vs. yellow/amber is also the pair that red-green color vision deficiencies merge. In practice I leave sessions waiting on input for a long time because I read the dot as "working" or "done".

### Proposal

Add a **Status colors** section to Settings → Appearance with a color picker for each of the four statuses and a "Reset to defaults" button. Defaults stay as they are today.

Implementation sketch (desktop only):
- A small persisted store holds optional hex overrides per status.
- The overrides are written to CSS variables (`--status-working`, `--status-permission`, `--status-failed`, `--status-review`) on `:root`; `StatusIndicator` and `DashboardSidebarAgentHoverRow` read those variables instead of fixed Tailwind classes, so every place that renders a status dot picks up the change.
- A settings-search entry so "status", "color", "colorblind" find it.

### Questions for maintainers

1. Persistence: a renderer `persist` store (like `markdown-preferences`) or the main-process settings that the `superset settings` CLI writes (like font settings)?
2. Would you also want a built-in colorblind-safe preset, or different defaults for "working" vs. "needs input"? I'm not proposing to change defaults in this PR unless you want that.

I'm happy to open the PR.

## Bug

The sidebar status indicators ("Running" and "Needs Input") are unreliable:

1. **Shows "Running" when not actually running** — the indicator stays lit even after the agent has stopped
2. **Shows "Needs Input" when there's no input needed** — false positives
3. **"Needs Input" doesn't show up when it should** — the agent is actually waiting for input but the sidebar doesn't reflect it

The behavior is intermittent/flaky — sometimes it works correctly, sometimes it doesn't.

## Expected behavior

- "Running" should only appear when the agent process is actively executing
- "Needs Input" should reliably appear whenever the agent is blocked waiting for user input
- Both indicators should clear promptly when the state changes

## Actual behavior

The indicators appear to be out of sync with the actual terminal process state. The detection seems unreliable — sometimes correct, sometimes wrong in either direction.

summary: 长会话缺少目录与跳转；该 issue 已关闭
body:
### Problem or motivation

cmux nails the "many agent sessions at once" problem (workspaces, splits, notification rings). The next pain point is navigating **inside** a single long session.

Once a Claude Code / Codex conversation grows to hundreds of turns, the only way back to an earlier exchange is blind scrolling through terminal scrollback. There is no overview of the conversation — no table of contents, no jump-to-message. "Find the part where we discussed X" currently means paging through thousands of unstructured lines.

### Proposed solution

A **session outline panel** (docked sidebar or floating overlay on the pane):

- Parse the active pane's conversation into a list of turns — primarily user prompts, optionally collapsed tool activity. The source of truth already exists on disk: Claude Code transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/*.jsonl`, and Codex session logs.
- Render turns as a compact outline (first line of each prompt + timestamp).
- **Clicking an entry scrolls the pane's scrollback to that exchange.** Only the terminal can implement this — it owns the scrollback buffer — which is why external transcript viewers can never close this loop, and why cmux is uniquely positioned.
- Live-update as the session grows; keyboard shortcut to toggle the panel.
- Bonus: badge turns containing errors or permission prompts.

cmux already parses agent output for notifications and already ingests Claude/Codex transcript files (per transcript-related work like #6993, #10677), so much of the groundwork seems to be in place.

### Alternatives considered

- Claude Code's built-in double-Esc rewind — keyboard-only, oriented to recent messages, no visual overview.
- External transcript viewers (claude-code-viewer, Switchboard, Claudes) — render an outline in a separate window, but can't scroll cmux's scrollback, so click-to-jump never completes.
- iTerm2 marks — keyboard jumping between shell prompts, no outline UI, not agent-aware.

### Additional context

- cmux 0.64.22 on macOS 14 (Apple Silicon iMac).
- This came out of a discussion among heavy terminal-agent users — the consensus was that no terminal currently offers conversation navigation, and the first one to build it wins the long-session workflow.
- Happy to help spec details or test an early build.

body:
### Feature request

Support saving the current set of open workspaces as a named session, and restoring it later, much like [tmux-resurrect](https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect) but for cmux workspace layouts.

### Motivation

I frequently have 4-6 workspaces open for a project context (monorepo services, infra, docs, etc). When I need to context-switch to a different project, I close everything and manually reopen. Being able to save/restore named sessions would make this instant.

Current session restore only covers the most recent state on relaunch — there's no way to go back to a previous workspace configuration or switch between saved setups.

### Suggested UX

```bash
cmux session save my-project
cmux session restore my-project
cmux session list
cmux session delete my-project
```

Each session would capture workspace count/order, working directories, and pane layout. 

### Related issues

- #399 — session restore race on launch
- #2072 — settings/tabs lost after macOS update (named session backups would also help here)
- #480 — persistence of tab information and pane layouts

summary: Windows 后台重启杀掉运行中的 Agent；单一环境报告
body:
## Environment

- Orca desktop 1.4.204 (Electron 43.7.0), Windows 11 Pro (x64), 48 GB RAM
- Main Orca process has been up for ~2 weeks; only the terminal host daemon restarts

## Summary

The terminal host daemon restarts silently and repeatedly under sustained load. Each restart recreates every terminal session, so every agent CLI running in an Orca terminal (Claude Code in my case) is killed mid-task, together with all of its child processes and background work.

Restart frequency jumped from about one per day to **6 restarts on 2026-10-29 and 8 on 2026-10-30**. The trigger looks similar to #19828, which was reported on macOS, but here no log entry explains any restart.

## Evidence (`%APPDATA%\Orca\logs\daemon.log`, UTC)

`"event":"startup"` entries with a new pid, plus the last event logged by the previous daemon:

| Daemon startup | Last event of the previous daemon | Live sessions before |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-29 13:56:11 | 13:51:22 session-killed | ~0 |
| 2026-10-29 14:00:18 | 13:56:12 session-created | ~0 |
| 2026-10-29 14:41:20 | 14:11:17 session-killed | ~0 |
| 2026-10-29 14:43:50 | 14:41:21 session-created | ~0 |
| 2026-10-29 15:00:01 | 14:57:40 session-created | ~3 |
| 2026-10-29 15:33:12 | 15:00:02 session-created | ~6 |
| 2026-10-30 01:39:42 | 01:21:48 session-killed | ~6 |
| 2026-10-30 01:56:57 | 01:39:43 session-created | ~9 |
| 2026-10-30 03:21:37 | 03:03:21 session-killed | ~8 |
| 2026-10-30 04:26:06 | 03:53:30 session-created | ~9 |
| 2026-10-30 05:20:03 | 04:26:07 session-created | ~11 |
| 2026-10-30 05:33:40 | 05:20:04 session-created | ~13 |
| 2026-10-30 05:54:49 | 05:33:42 session-created | ~15 |
| 2026-10-30 05:58:50 | 05:56:47 session-created | ~19 |

"Live sessions" is a rough count derived from created/exited/killed events in the same log, so it is approximate.

- In every case the old daemon logs **no** shutdown, exit, error or signal event before it disappears.
- `crash-reports.json` has no entry for these restarts. The only entries there are older renderer `killed` reports.
- The Windows Application event log has no error entries for Orca or node in the same window.
- After each restart, sessions are recreated with `startup-command-delivery ... "written":false`. In the Orca CLI, every terminal reappears under a **new handle**. Terminals created with `orca terminal create --command "claude"` come back as a bare shell attempting to resume a conversation id that does not exist.

## Workload at the time

- 2 to 4 Claude Code sessions in Orca terminals, each running long multi-agent jobs.
- The agents spawned many child processes inside those terminal trees: Vite dev servers (~0.5-1 GB each), headless Chromium via Playwright, and `pnpm install` in git worktrees.
- Peak was roughly 10 concurrent agents. Free RAM measured between 6 and 12 GB of 48 GB, so the host was not out of memory. I did not capture per-process memory at the exact moment of a restart.

## Expected

- A heavy or crashing child process inside one terminal should not take down the daemon and every other terminal.
- If the daemon must die, it should log why: an exit code, uncaught exception or OOM marker in `daemon.log`.

## Workaround

Long-running agent jobs survive when launched outside Orca's process tree, as a separate console window started via `explorer.exe`. That is consistent with the daemon tearing down its whole session tree on restart.

Related: #19828 (same cascade on macOS), #21343, #20083, #18482.

body:
## Ask

Support workspaces that contain **multiple git repositories**, so users can view diffs across several repos side-by-side without switching workspaces.

Today, each Orca workspace is scoped to a single repo/worktree. Users working on changes that span multiple repos (e.g. frontend + backend, or service + shared library) have to switch between workspaces to see each repo's diff.

## Desired behavior

- A workspace can include more than one repo root
- Source Control shows each repo's changes as a separate region within the same workspace (similar to multi-root workspaces in VS Code)
- Terminal, file tree, and diff views understand the multi-repo layout

## Notes

This is a large feature — touches the worktree model, Source Control UI, diff aggregation, and per-repo git state. Filing to collect upvotes and gauge demand.

summary: 希望看到派单上下文的构成和膨胀
body:
### Problem or use case

### English

In a fresh Orca-dispatched Claude worker, the per-request input footprint grew from **37,156 tokens** on the first request and about **38,283** on the second to **105,567 within roughly ten minutes**. It reached **127,935** near the end of the session.

These numbers are `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` for individual requests, **not cumulative billing or total spend**.

**Observed facts:**
- This was a new session; no old conversation was resumed.
- Unrelated project MCP servers had already been disabled.
- The run coordinated Claude, Kimi, and the official DeepSeek Harness, but there is no evidence that another worker's context was merged into Claude's.
- New-session tool output totalled about **196,105 characters**. The largest outputs were about **25,767**, **23,371**, and **14,164** characters. Three source reads were about **13,104**, **12,960**, and **10,856** characters. Character counts are output sizes only; I am not converting them to token counts.

**Likely contributors, based on the transcript rather than a category-level token measurement:**
- a large startup payload from global/project instructions, tool schemas, skill listings, and Orca dispatch guidance;
- large source reads and diffs retained across turns;
- verbose Orca JSON and terminal snapshots, including repeated long output after failed commands.

What is missing is a per-role way to constrain startup context and tool output, plus visibility into which context category is growing before compaction. This overlaps with #30764, #36221, #35557, #29107, #20395, #22477, and #11225; this report adds measured growth from one fresh dispatched-worker session.

### 中文

一个全新的 Orca 派单 Claude Worker 中，单次请求输入从首次 **37,156 tokens**、第二次约 **38,283**，在约十分钟内增长到 **105,567**，会话末期达到 **127,935**。

以上数值是单次请求的 `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens`，**不是累计账单或总花费**。

**已观测事实：**
- 这是全新会话，没有恢复旧对话。
- 无关的项目级 MCP 已禁用。
- 本次编排包含 Claude、Kimi 和官方 DeepSeek Harness，但没有证据表明其他 Worker 的上下文被合并进 Claude。
- 新会话工具输出累计约 **196,105 字符**，最大的几次约为 **25,767、23,371、14,164 字符**；三次源码读取约为 **13,104、12,960、10,856 字符**。字符数只表示输出大小，不换算为 token。

**根据会话记录判断的可能原因（并非分类 token 实测）：**
- 全局/项目指令、工具 schema、技能目录及 Orca 派单指南形成较高的启动上下文；
- 大型源码读取和 diff 跨轮保留；
- 冗长的 Orca JSON、终端画面及失败命令的重复长输出。

目前缺少按角色限制启动上下文和工具输出的能力，也缺少在压缩前定位上下文增长来源的可观测性。本问题与上述 Issue 有重叠，但补充了一个全新派单 Worker 会话中的实测增长数据。


### Proposed solution

### English

1. **Role-scoped worker profiles:** allow a dispatch to declare the tools, MCP servers, skills, and orchestration instructions a worker actually needs. A read-only reviewer should not receive coordinator-only APIs or the full skill catalog.
2. **Concise dispatch preambles:** provide a short task contract and an explicit opt-in for the full orchestration guide, rather than injecting the complete guide into every worker.
3. **Tool-output budgets:** support configurable size limits, pagination, and structured summaries for source reads, diffs, JSON, and terminal snapshots. Preserve exit codes, errors, and truncation markers so nothing is silently omitted.
4. **Context observability:** expose estimated tokens by category (instructions, tool schemas, skills, dispatch preamble, messages, and tool results), with a configurable warning/checkpoint threshold before automatic compaction.
5. **Orca-native configuration:** make the workspace workaround discussed in #30764 available as a reusable per-role Orca setting, so users do not have to hand-edit each workspace.

### 中文

1. **按角色配置 Worker：**派单时声明该 Worker 实际需要的工具、MCP、技能和编排指令；只读复核角色不应获得协调者专用 API 或完整技能目录。
2. **精简派单 preamble：**默认提供简短任务契约，完整编排指南改为显式按需加载，避免注入每个 Worker。
3. **工具输出预算：**为源码读取、diff、JSON 和终端画面提供可配置的大小限制、分页和结构化摘要；保留退出码、错误及截断标记，不能静默省略。
4. **上下文可观测性：**按指令、工具 schema、技能、派单 preamble、消息和工具结果分类展示估算 token，并在自动压缩前提供可配置的预警或检查点阈值。
5. **Orca 原生配置：**将 #30764 中的工作区级替代方案做成可复用的分角色 Orca 配置，避免用户逐个手工修改工作区。


### Alternatives or additional context

### English

**Environment:** Windows 11, Orca **1.4.243**, an Orca-managed Claude Code worker coordinating Kimi and official DeepSeek Harness workers.

**Workarounds tried:**
- disabled unrelated project MCP servers before starting the new session;
- later limited source reads to about 150 lines and command output to about 6,000 characters;
- asked the worker to write a short checkpoint around 120k tokens instead of waiting for automatic compaction.

These reduced further reading but did not prevent the earlier growth. The workspace settings approach in #30764 is relevant, but it is manual and workspace-wide rather than role-scoped per dispatch. I have not verified a complete workaround.

The measurements above come from real client request usage and local session output sizes. I have intentionally omitted session IDs, terminal handles, local configuration, and credentials.

### 中文

**环境：**Windows 11，Orca **1.4.243**，由 Orca 管理的 Claude Code Worker 协调 Kimi 和官方 DeepSeek Harness Worker。

**已尝试的替代办法：**
- 在新会话启动前禁用无关的项目级 MCP；
- 后续将源码读取限制在约 150 行、命令输出限制在约 6,000 字符；
- 要求 Worker 在约 120k tokens 时先写简短检查点，而不是等待自动压缩。

这些措施减少了后续扩读，但没有阻止此前已经发生的增长。#30764 的工作区配置方案有参考价值，但它是手工、工作区级配置，不是按派单角色隔离。目前尚未验证出完整的替代方案。

以上数据来自真实客户端请求用量和本地会话输出大小；报告已主动排除会话 ID、终端 handle、本地配置和凭据。

### Problem or use case

On Windows, Orca sometimes becomes unresponsive and the main window shows "Not Responding". It seems to happen when starting a new chat or invoking a skill, but I do not yet have a reliable reproduction. The problem persisted after a clean reinstall.

Newer versions feel heavier than earlier releases in my usual environment, but I have not benchmarked versions side by side and cannot establish that an update caused the issue.

Environment: Windows, Orca 1.4.244, and Kaspersky Endpoint Security. During a freeze, the main window was reported as Responding=False and its UI thread used little CPU. Some Git operations in Orca's trace took 17?25 seconds, but their connection to the freeze is unconfirmed. IT has configured an exclusion for the Orca data folder; its effective application on this device has not been verified.

Has anyone else experienced freezes or increased resource usage after updating? What diagnostics would help identify what the UI is waiting for?


### Proposed solution

Please consider a lightweight mode or configurable performance options that preserve responsiveness as Orca gains new features:

- Reduce or make configurable background Git polling and file watching.
- Limit work performed by inactive sessions and load skills or other features on demand.
- Benchmark CPU, memory, and disk I/O across releases for common workflows such as multiple sessions, starting a chat, and invoking a skill.
- Add diagnostics for an unresponsive window that help identify what the main/UI thread is doing or waiting for.

The goal is to keep Orca responsive in the same environments across updates, including machines with corporate endpoint security.


### Alternatives or additional context

Potentially related reports (the cause may be different):
- https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/26027 ? closed; reports Windows UI freezes with endpoint security in an older Orca version.
- https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/7175 ? open; reports Windows unresponsiveness with multiple concurrent sessions.

I have not confirmed whether the present hang shares either root cause.

summary: 多个项目与约 20 个 TUI 下输入停顿
body:
Request: make sidebar refresh cost stop scaling with workspace and host count. Typing in terminals stalls every 2-3 s on a fast, mostly idle Mac.

Setup (desktop 1.35.0, macOS arm64, M5 Pro, 18 cores, 48 GB, no swap):
209 workspaces across 7 paired hosts (57 local, the rest remote over the relay), about 20 agent TUIs running.

Measured (renderer process only):
Average 59-64% of one core over 30 s.
Sampled every 0.5 s: 30-40% baseline with bursts of 100-170% every 2-3 s. The bursts line up with the typing stalls.
Renderer network is small (about 12.5 KB/s in, 7.5 KB/s out), so this is CPU on the main thread, not data volume.
The IndexedDB store holding `superset-rq-cache` is 9.9 MB.
Lowering `terminalParkedRuntimeCap` from 12 to 3 changed nothing. Alt-screen TUIs are exempt from eviction (`terminal-runtime-registry.ts`), so the cap never applies to agent panes.

What the code does at desktop-v1.35.0:
`ElectronTRPCProvider.tsx` persists the `dashboard-sidebar` query keys (plus tasks, PR/issue detail, host.roster, cloudWorkspace.list) through `PersistQueryClientProvider` into IndexedDB, serialized with superjson.
TanStack's persist client re-runs `dehydrate()` over the whole cache on every query-cache added/updated/removed event, synchronously, before the throttled write. (I read this in @tanstack/query-persist-client-core but have not profiled it.)
`DashboardSidebarWorkspaceStatusProvider.tsx` runs one `terminalAgents.listByWorkspace` query per sidebar workspace with a `refetchInterval`, so 209 queries keep the cache churning. That is 209 dehydrate passes over a large cache.
`AsciiSpinner.tsx` runs a `setInterval` per working row, which means a React re-render per spinner at a fixed tick.
Collapsed groups are still included in the status set (DashboardSidebar `orderedGroups` ignores collapse). Only hidden projects are excluded.

Proposed changes, ranked by expected impact:
1. Persist on a trailing timer (for example 30 s, and on `visibilitychange`/quit) instead of per cache event. Or drop `dashboard-sidebar` from `PERSIST_KEY_PREFIXES`. Either keeps dehydrate off the hot path.
2. Replace the 209 per-workspace `listByWorkspace` queries with the per-host batched agent list (one query per host).
3. Move the spinner to a CSS `steps()` animation so a working row costs no JS ticks.
4. Make per-host refetch intervals adaptive: fast for the host with the active workspace, slow (60 s+) for others, and off while `document.hidden`.
5. Skip collapsed groups in the status provider.

Mitigations I am applying meanwhile: hiding inactive projects and keeping the resource monitor closed (it polls every 2 s while open).
